answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each new agent to complete a timed zephyr challenge: it must bridge a cryptographic canyon by generating a unique proof-of-work solution that incorporates a random seed from the previous epoch's honest majority, with the difficulty scaling linearly with recent registration volume. This forces an attacker to expend proportionally more CPU cycles and electricity per fake identity, while honest agents pay only a fixed baseline cost, making large-scale identity farming economically unviable beyond a small number of nodes.
